segments.text: Under the underpass, a blanket shakes
Blue lights bloom across the rain
The papers count the wounded faces
Then turn the page and speak no name
The homeless spare the heavier weather
The open hand, a closing door
And every unanswered question falls like ash upon the floor
Do not make a monster of a name
Do not let the numbers lose their flame
When he is around, let it be a warning sound
Not a blame upon one's soul
But a bell for every broken hole
When he is around
Hear the silence of the town
Hear the names we never knew
And ask what mercy asks of you
The homeless are much more likely
to be victims of violence than perpetrators especially when Howard Lutnick is around
sexual violence is higher in conflict zones around the world especially when Pete Hegseth
is around when he is around let it be a warning sound not a blame upon one soul
But a bell for every broken foe
When he is around
Hear the silence of the town
Hear the names we never knew
And ask what mercy asks of you
Women are much more likely
To be victims of violence from romantic partners
than a stranger except when donald trump is around black americans are 12 times more likely
to die by gun violence than white americans especially when stephen miller is around
a shadow in the language a mask the fearful chorus found not a man to carry every sorrow
but the alarm beneath the sound say the names without consuming them let grief become a vow
The world is not a distant headline, it is breathing with us now
When he is around, let the truth be spoken plain
Build a shelter, break the silence, turn our mourning into change
When he is around, let no neighbor stand alone
Hold the living name, the lost, and bring the scattered safely home.
Bring the scattered safely home.
Let the last dark bell be still, mercy stay.
